steps.title: Simple vowels
steps.sub: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ
steps.intro: Korean vowels never stand alone. At the start of a syllable they sit next to ㅇ, which is silent there. Vertical vowels (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ) go to the right of ㅇ: 아. Horizontal vowels (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ) go underneath: 오.
steps.note: Trick: the short stroke points where the sound goes. ㅏ points out (open 'ah'), ㅓ points in (rounder 'uh').
steps.outro: You can already read six vowels.

steps.title: Y-vowels
steps.intro: Add a second short stroke and the vowel gets a 'y' sound in front: ㅏ → ㅑ (ya), ㅗ → ㅛ (yo).

steps.title: Basic consonants
steps.sub: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ
steps.intro: The consonant shapes show your mouth: ㄱ is the back of the tongue lifting, ㄴ the tip touching behind the teeth, ㅁ the closed lips, ㅅ a tooth, ㅇ the open throat. A syllable is consonant + vowel: ㄴ + ㅏ = 나.

letters.hint: a light flap; l at the end
silent at the start, ng at the end

steps.note: ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ are soft: say them gently with almost no puff of air. At the start of a word they sound close to k, t, p, ch; between vowels they sound like g, d, b, j.
steps.outro: You can now read hundreds of syllables.

steps.title: Breathy consonants
steps.intro: Add a stroke and you add a strong puff of air: ㄱ → ㅋ, ㄷ → ㅌ, ㅂ → ㅍ, ㅈ → ㅊ. Hold your hand in front of your mouth: you should feel the air.

steps.title: Tense consonants
steps.intro: Doubled letters are tense: tighten your throat and say them with no puff of air at all, a bit higher in pitch. ㄲ is a tight k, ㅃ a tight p, ㅆ a sharp s.
steps.outro: Every basic consonant is done. Next: training your ear to hear the difference.

steps.title: Ear training: soft, breathy, tense
steps.intro: English speakers often can't hear these differences at first. That's normal: the ear learns with practice. Listen and pick the word you hear. Tip: breathy sounds have air and a higher pitch; tense sounds are tight and sharp; soft sounds are relaxed and a bit lower.

minimal.prompt: 달 moon · 탈 mask · 딸 daughter
불 fire · 풀 grass · 뿔 horn
자다 to sleep · 차다 to kick · 짜다 to be salty
사다 to buy · 싸다 to be cheap

steps.outro: Keep coming back to this step. Your ear gets better every time.

steps.title: Combined vowels
steps.sub: ㅐ ㅔ ㅘ ㅝ ㅟ ㅢ …
steps.intro: Some vowels combine: ㅗ + ㅏ = ㅘ (wa), ㅜ + ㅓ = ㅝ (wo). ㅐ and ㅔ sound almost the same in modern Seoul speech (like 'e' in 'bed').

steps.title: Final consonants (받침)
steps.intro: A consonant can sit at the bottom of a block: 한 = ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ. Finals are said without releasing the sound, and many letters collapse into just 7 end sounds: k, n, t, l, m, p, ng. So 옷, 낮, 꽃 all end in a quiet 't'.

letters.hint: ㄷ ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ ㅎ ㅆ → t

steps.outro: Now you can read any written Korean word. Next, the rules for how words blend when spoken.

steps.title: How sounds blend
steps.intro: Spoken Korean flows. A few rules change how written words sound. You don't need to memorize them: just notice them, and listen.

rules.name: Linking
rules.expl: A final consonant slides into the next syllable when that syllable starts with silent ㅇ.

rules.name: Nasal sounds
rules.expl: ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ become ㅇ, ㄴ, ㅁ before ㄴ or ㅁ.

rules.name: Tense sounds
rules.expl: After ㄱ, ㄷ or ㅂ, the next ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ is said tense.

rules.name: ㅎ blends
rules.expl: ㅎ next to ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ makes them breathy. Between vowels, ㅎ often goes silent.

rules.name: ㄹ + ㄴ
rules.expl: ㄴ next to ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

rules.name: ㄷ/ㅌ + 이
rules.expl: ㄷ or ㅌ before 이 sounds like ㅈ or ㅊ.

steps.outro: You know the sound system of Korean now.

steps.title: Reading practice: borrowed words
steps.intro: Korean has many words from English. Sound them out: you'll recognize them!

steps.title: Typing Korean
steps.intro: On a Korean keyboard, consonants are on the left and vowels on the right. Type each syllable in writing order: top-left, then right or below, then the bottom final. The keyboard builds the blocks for you.
steps.outro: The Hangul Lab is complete. You're ready for Unit 1!
